claim:
Let \(X=\mathrm{ces}_2^{(2)}\) be the real plane with
\[
\|(x,y)\|_X=
\left(x^2+\left(\frac{|x|+|y|}{2}\right)^2\right)^{1/2}.
\]
For \(\varepsilon\in[0,1)\), write \(u\perp_D^\varepsilon v\) when
\[
\|u+\lambda v\|_X\ge \sqrt{1-\varepsilon^2}\,\|u\|_X
\qquad(\lambda\in\mathbb R).
\]
Then the least \(\varepsilon\) for which \(x\perp_B y\) implies \(y\perp_D^\varepsilon x\) for all \(x,y\in X\) is
\[
\varepsilon_D(X)=\sqrt{\frac38}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\inf_{\substack{x,y\in S_X\\x\perp_B y}}\inf_{\lambda\in\mathbb R}\|y+\lambda x\|_X=\sqrt{\frac58}.
\]
After the linear normalization \(M(s,t)=\sqrt{s^2+t^2+2|st|/\sqrt5}\), equality is attained by
\[
x=(1,0),\qquad y=\frac{(1/\sqrt5,1)}{\sqrt{8/5}},
\]
and its norm symmetries.

correctness.rationale: Exact normalization gives M(s,t)^2=s^2+t^2+2|st|/sqrt(5). Smooth Birkhoff pairs reduce to one parameter; Euclidean point-to-line distance is a lower bound for M-distance and the exact residual identity is 4z^2/5 above the 5/8 threshold. Axis points have complete cone |a|<=|b|/sqrt(5), and a boundary cone direction realizes equality.
risks: The result uses the modified Dragomir normalization sqrt(1-epsilon^2), not the original 1-epsilon normalization.

value.rationale: Approximate symmetry quantitatively measures failure of Birkhoff--James orthogonality to be symmetric. General literature proves existence of a modified-Dragomir parameter in finite dimensions; this theorem supplies a sharp exact benchmark on a classical Cesàro plane and shows that the worst reverse asymmetry occurs at a boundary direction of a nonsmooth axis cone, while smooth pairs have strict surplus.
risks: This is one canonical two-dimensional benchmark rather than a general Cesàro-exponent formula.
